question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Fair-weather friends

options.text: A person who is friends with you during the night
A person who is friends with you every day
A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in times
A person who is friends with you in difficult times

solution:
The correct answer is option 3), i.e., "A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in times."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let’s look at the meaning of the given idiom/ phrase: 
 
• The idiom **"fair-weather friends" **refers to people who are only your friends during good times but not reliable or trustworthy in a difficult situation. (ऐसे लोग जो केवल अच्छे समय के दौरान आपके मित्र होते हैं लेकिन कठिन परिस्थिति में विश्वसनीय या भरोसेमंद नहीं होते हैं)
 
• *Example*:
 
 
• *​People he had trusted turned out to be only **fair-weather friends.***
 
 
 
• Hence, the only possible answer is option 3, 'A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in times,' which exactly resembles the meaning of the given idiom/ phrase.

 

Correct meaning:__ *A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in times.*
